$comment: Control-plane asset_id LINEAGE MANIFEST, authorised by ADHIKĀRIN as D-103 (state/DECISIONS.jsonl), closing PARIKSAKA V-67 / F-V67-1. NOT A SCHEMA CHANGE (D-103 part 5 is explicit) — this is a committed JSON file, Track M registry metadata, following the same pattern as unearned_lit_floor.json / entrypoint_guard_floor.json / asset_catalogue_disclosed_residuals.json in this directory. It exists because `build_run_assets.asset_id` has no FK to `asset_registry.asset_id` and asset_ids can move (rename, deletion, or a caller naming an asset that was never valid) with NOTHING queryable recording the move — D-103's framing, third variant of the same shape as D-94 (row leaving a population by changing category) and D-99 (an agent indistinguishable from another by sharing a name) found earlier the same evening. Every entry below is DERIVED from a migration file, a live (read-only) database query, or a cited doctrine/closure artifact — never hand-guessed (D-67 part 4 discipline, extended here by analogy per D-103 part 3). This file does NOT change which side any ratchet or gate anchors on: `check_asset_catalogue_contract.py` x06() still anchors on `asset_registry` alone (see that function's doc-comment, amended by this same task, D-103 part 6). This manifest is descriptive lineage metadata; nothing reads it yet (see `not_yet_wired_for_resolution` below for the reasoning, D-103 part 5).

disposition_vocabulary.renamed: The old asset_id was UPDATEd to a new asset_id by a specific, cited migration. asset_registry now carries the new id; build_run_assets rows under the old id are real evidence of real historical builds and refer to the SAME asset under its earlier name.
disposition_vocabulary.deleted: The asset_id was DELETEd from asset_registry by a specific, cited migration and is not superseded by any other id — the asset itself was retired, not renamed.
disposition_vocabulary.legacy_never_registered: No migration, at any point in this repository's history, ever inserted this exact string as an asset_registry.asset_id. Any build_run_assets/build_runs rows under it are evidence of a REQUEST for something that was never a valid registry asset, not evidence of a real asset's history.

entries.summary: GOCHARA-UTKARSA W6.4 (UTK-R2) cutover. Migration 563 (a) deletes the old zero-row 'ka_gochara' global-scope self-test row that occupied that id, (b) inserts a new asset_registry row under asset_id='ka_gochara' copied from 'ka_gochara_v2_materialize' with its identity fields overridden, (c) repoints every FK-referencing child row (asset_throughput.asset_id, asset_coefficients.{upstream,downstream}_asset_id) from the old id to the new one, then (d) drops the old 'ka_gochara_v2_materialize' asset_registry row. THE MECHANISM THAT PRODUCED PARIKSAKA'S FALSE-POSITIVE RISK: step (c) repoints asset_throughput — the table asset_kind/lit-state checks read — but does NOT touch build_run_assets, which has no FK to asset_registry and was never in the migration's scope. So build_run_assets legitimately and permanently retains 'ka_gochara_v2_materialize' as the asset_id for builds that ran before the rename, while asset_registry and asset_throughput both now only know the asset as 'ka_gochara'. A naive join of build_run_assets to asset_registry on asset_id therefore reports zero completed builds for 'ka_gochara' even though real, recent, successful builds exist under its pre-rename name.

'chart_dashas' is instead the TARGET_TABLE of the real, currently-registered asset_id 'ga_dashas' (migration 217_ga_count_sql_reconcile.sql repoints ga_dashas's target_table + count_sql to chart_dashas; asset_registry_seed.ts's ga_dashas entry carries the same comment: 'ga_dashas writer (GA7) writes to chart_dashas, not ganita_dashas (empty). Repointed in migration 217.'). Live DB inspection of the actual build_runs rows behind all 3 build_run_assets 'chart_dashas' entries shows they are NOT independent historical incidents: all 3 belong to build_runs created on 2026-06-26 against chart_id 1c826d5a-41cb-4450-b4dc-59d440e5f75a (Abhinandan Mohanty — the Phase E operator-E2E chart named in L1_GANITA_CLOSURE), triggered by the same principal (uid xl2wYZRPwsVgPSAgtn9XJ80Xkub2), each with 'chart_dashas' sitting in the run's own `plan` jsonb array as a distinct planned step (never as a `scope_target`). This is caller-supplied plan data, not registry data — the best-supported reading is that the table's highly-visible name ('chart_dashas' appears in the cockpit, in migration 217, and throughout writer/reader code) was used by whatever build-request path was in play that day in place of the registered asset_id 'ga_dashas'. The disposition is 'legacy_never_registered' rather than a guess at 'renamed', because no registry row named 'chart_dashas' ever existed to be renamed FROM.

entries.summary: ga_chart_service is confirmed a REAL, LIVE, RUNNING service (platform/python-sidecar/brahmagyan/ganita/engine.py), consulted synchronously by retrieval-layer code today — it is genuinely running. It was, however, NEVER RENAMED and NEVER REGISTERED IN asset_registry, under this id or any other kind. Evidence for each of the three possibilities ADHIKĀRIN named: (1) NOT RENAMED — no migration renames anything to or from 'ga_chart_service' (grep across every migration for the literal string: zero hits touching asset_registry). (2) NOT REGISTERED UNDER ANOTHER KIND — a live query of every asset_kind='service' row in asset_registry today (8 rows: bg_ephemeris_engine, bg_panchanga, ka_dasha_kala, ka_graha_sancara, ka_muhurta_seva, ka_tulana, mi_abhilekha, mi_seva) contains no L1/Gaṇita chart-service row under any id — there is no service-kind row that IS ga_chart_service wearing a different name. (3) GENUINELY NEVER REGISTERED, AND THIS APPEARS TO BE BY DELIBERATE DESIGN, NOT AN OVERSIGHT — L1_GANITA_CLOSURE_v1_0.md (2026-06-12, now SUPERSEDED) §2.1 briefly listed `ga_chart_service` in its 10-row asset table as '(service; no direct table)', alongside the 9 real registered ga_* rows, but its successor L1_GANITA_CLOSURE_v2_0.md (2026-06-18, CURRENT) §2.1's 'full 15-asset picture' DROPS it entirely — between the two seals the decision was made not to carry it in asset_registry. RETRIEVAL_STRATEGY_v1_0.md §5.3 ('Service-asset coverage', a native ruling dated 2026-07-19) then formalises this as doctrine: 'Coverage is stored assets + service assets. The plane's second data source is real-time computation — ga_chart_service, the panchanga service, the ephemeris/python sidecars ... Computed responses carry their own provenance honesty: computed_at, engine/ephemeris version — the real-time analogue of build_id (they cannot carry one).' A service that computes on demand and cannot carry a build_id is doctrinally a different kind of thing than an asset_registry row, and ga_chart_service is the named example of that category. The single build_run_assets row for it is a stray artifact of one operator build-request attempt (build_runs id 92133010-9f35-43b6-b126-552cb8dc9b8f, action='build', scope_target='ga_chart_service', chart_id=1c826d5a-41cb-4450-b4dc-59d440e5f75a, created 2026-06-26T15:31:48Z, run state='failed') — the SAME day and SAME operator-E2E chart as the 3 chart_dashas rows above, consistent with one operator session attempting to trigger builds of things named in v1.0's closure-doc asset table that were never actually registry rows.

not_yet_wired_for_resolution: D-103 part 5 asks that this task CONSIDER, and state reasoning either way, whether x06() (or any other rule) should READ this manifest to resolve renamed ids (e.g. crediting ka_gochara_v2_materialize's completed builds to ka_gochara). REASONING: x06()'s 'ran' set is built as `{r['asset_id'] for r in build_run_assets if state=='complete'}` and then tested for membership by the CURRENT registry asset_id only (`aid in ran`, where aid iterates s.assets, i.e. asset_registry). Making it rename-aware would require, at minimum: (a) loading this manifest, (b) for every 'renamed' entry, unioning the old id's complete-run evidence into the new id's membership test, and (c) deciding what happens if the OLD id ALSO still exists as a distinct row somewhere in a snapshot (it should not, post-rename, but that is an assumption this task did not verify against every possible snapshot shape). That is more than a one-line addition to a function whose doc-comment already carries five ADHIKĀRIN rulings' worth of accumulated invariants (D-42, D-87, D-94, D-95, D-84) — the risk of silently breaking one of those invariants while wiring in rename-resolution is exactly the kind of confident-but-wrong change D-103's own defect (a confident false accusation) warns against one level up. RECOMMENDATION (not implemented this task): a follow-up task, scoped ONLY to x06(), should (1) load this manifest, (2) for each 'renamed' entry add the old id to the `ran` set lookup for the new id specifically (not touch anything else in the function), and (3) add a dedicated fixture asserting ka_gochara's completed ka_gochara_v2_materialize builds now correctly clear it of the unearned-lit flag. Filed as a recommendation, not built here, per this task's explicit instruction to stop and report rather than restructure x06()'s core logic.
